newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: UPS to fly 6 times a week to Philippines.
newsitem.headline: UPS to fly 6 times a week to Philippines.

text.p: U.S. cargo carrier United Parcel Services will start flying six times a week to the Philippines, UPS regional vice president for Asia Pacific Charles Adams said on Tuesday.

Manila will be one of the supporting units to UPS' Asian hub based in Taipei. Most of the flights will fly in during the night to avoid the growing passenger traffic at Manila's Ninoy Aquino International Airport, Adams said.
UPS expects cargoes in and out of Manila to fill six to eight container slots out of the 18 slots available in its DC-8 cargo airplanes.
Its rival Federal Express Corp has set up its Asian hub inside the Subic free port area, north of Manila.
UPS was allowed to fly into the Philippines under a new air accord signed with the United States late last year.
Since then, UPS has earmarked $82 million to open its operations in the Philippines.
It had established its Asian accounting and information services in Manila and had formed a joint venture with local transportation firm Delbros Inc to operate a trucking service company.
"We anticipate that over the next three to five years, we will expand our operations in Manila," Adams told Reuters.
